summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with chronic pancreatitis and a history of sphincter of Oddi dysfunction was admitted with a two-day history of epigastric pain worsened by eating, along with nausea and vomiting. She was managed for an acute flare of chronic pancreatitis with bowel rest, IV fluids, and symptom control. Lipase was initially elevated but trended downward, and imaging showed no obstruction or free air. Her diet was gradually advanced to low-fat solids, and she remained asymptomatic. Drowsiness on admission, likely due to medication effects, improved with dose adjustments. A positive amphetamine tox screen was considered a probable false positive. She was discharged home in stable condition with plans to follow up with her gastroenterologist for an outpatient MRCP with secretin and medication review.
